thread:
diego: flagging a weird spike in the per-model ROI card after we enabled sticky-routing for sessionized flows. several tenants show model_family 'redwood-7b' with negative net cost (savings > spend).
meera: hmm, negative net cost? screenshot? did the rollout change prefetch amortization window?
diego: screenshot attached. looks like our amortized prefetch credits are being applied across sessions after sticky-routing extended affinity. truncated debug: ```session_id=abc123, tenant=beta-corp, model_family=redwood-7b, prefetch_alloc=5, amortized_window=30m, billed_tokens=40```
olga: sticky-routing will keep a session pinned to a hotpath; if amortization window is per-session but credits were originally allocated to a previous session id, we could double-apply when affinity moves.
meera: interesting. current algorithm: when a prefetch is consumed we mark credits amortized across the next N minutes by tenant+route. sticky-routing changed route affinity key to include session_id, so the amortization lookup misses and we create new amortization buckets. net effect: same prefetch counted twice across bucket boundaries.
diego: that matches what I see. how invasive is the fix? two options: 1) change amortization key back to tenant+route (coarser) so sticky-routing doesn't fragment buckets; 2) keep session_id but emit reconciliation traces and compensating amortization adjustments when we detect duplicate allocation.
olga: option 1 reduces cardinality and fixes heatmap quickly but loses per-session granularity product liked. option 2 is safer for correctness long-term but needs compensating logic and reconciliation latency.
meera: also telemetry concern: console needs to show if amortization is "sessioned" or "global" per-tenant so users understand why numbers change after routing rules. product asked for explicit label in the ROI card.
diego: API/metrics debate: do we change the amortizer service to emit `amortize.assign` + `amortize.adjust` events, or keep assigns only and handle duplicates in analytics?
olga: for ops' ability to reconcile, we should emit both. `amortize.assign { tenant, model_family, bucket_key, amount, session_id? }` and `amortize.adjust { tenant, model_family, bucket_key, delta, reason }`. consumers can compute net easily. keep session_id optional to avoid high-cardinality when absent.
meera: agree. also we should add a short-run alert: if amortized credits across distinct bucket_keys for a tenant exceed tenant_spend * 0.2 in 10m, ping econ-ops. that'll catch regressions quickly.
diego: UX: ROI card will show a small badge "sessioned amortization" when session_id used, and a hover with a one-line explanation and link to docs. product prefers not to bury this.
olga: implementation plan: 1) emit adjust events from amortizer when sticky-routing causes detected duplication (fast path); 2) change default bucket_key to tenant+route unless tenant has enabled sessioned amortization; 3) add console label + alert.
meera: migration notes: metrics pipeline must map session_id -> flag only, not full id, to reduce cardinality. keep full session ids in 0.5% audit stream.
diego: rolling canary planned: amortizer-v2 -> canary infra-d in 20m. I'll open a short runbook for econ-ops with query snippets for net vs gross and duplicate-bucket searches.
ingest-bot: canary started: amortizer-v2 on infra-d (5% traffic) :rocket:
meera: thanks. olga, can you mock the badge copy? Diego, I'll own the alert rule and metric definitions.
olga: will do. quick draft: badge text "Sessioned amortization active" tooltip: "Credits are amortized per session affinity; numbers may shift if routing rules change."
diego: perfect. will post runbook link in #eng-platform when canary metrics stabilize. ping @eng-sre and @product for visibility.
ingest-bot: canary success -> rolling to 25% after 12m :white_check_mark:
diego: moving to merge and monitor overnight. good catch everyone.
